long adjective

in length

also longer

classical

Liv. 21.28.7: ducentōs longam pedēs
Cic. Att. 16.11: longissima epistula (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 204
Traupman 341

longus, longa, longum

adjective, declension

A length goes in the accusative: septem pedēs longus, seven feet long (Plin. NH 6.212, Lewis & Short). Of a person, longus is a colloquial “lanky” (Catull. 67.47, Lewis & Short). For a long time, see long (for a long time).

Examples

  • ratem ūnam ducentōs longam pedēs, quīnquāgintā lātam ā terrā in amnem porrēxērunt

    they ran a raft two hundred feet long and fifty wide out from the bank into the riverLiv. 21.28.7

  • omnia ista in longā vītā sunt, quōmodo in longā viā et pulvis et lutum et pluvia

    all that comes with a long life, as dust, mud and rain come with a long roadSen. Ep. 96.3

  • quīndecim mīlia passuum in longitūdinem patēns

    fifteen miles longTraupman 204–205

  • Vōcālis est longa nātūrā aut positiōne.

    A vowel is long by nature or by position.Traupman 341

See also long, long-sleeved.
